content:
I'm curious about the upcoming formatter in general, and also about what it means for linters. :) Namely:

  1. How opinionated will the formatter be? Will it normalize primarily whitespace, or also things like parentheses, identifier namespacing, pipe projection...? What will it deliberately stay silent on? Will there be escape hatches to override it in certain settings?
  2. How extensible will it be? For example, will it be able to support the addition of new rules like "align the rows and columns of Mathlib's custom matrix syntax according to custom rules"?
  3. Will metaprograms like linters be able to hook into it? One example of a possible use case I encountered recently is refactoring a bare function application of an identifier, say Foo A B C, into custom notation that infers some arguments or otherwise assists elaboration, say Foo[B] (Bar% C), and providing the new syntax as an interactive suggestion. But maybe we need to check to see if the notation actually succeeds, and detect if Bar% is really necessary—things we must test in an elaboration-aware setting like a linter. We can do this presently, but ideally we don't want to just delaborate B and C again to construct our suggestion; we'd really like to preserve the stylistic choices of the original syntax within B and C to some extent, except if we want to reformat them to handle new (shorter) line lengths and changed parenthesization. I could imagine a formatting framework that metaprograms could use to transform the syntax "respectfully".
